chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Hamzah al-Qummi from Zakariyya ibn Adam who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'I prohibit you from the slaughtered meat of everyone who is in opposition to the belief upon which you and your companions are, except in the time of necessity for it. And the second aspect is that these narrations came in the place of Taqiyya (dissimulation), because all those who opposed us consider its permissibility, and that which indicates that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of non-Shia Muslims according to Imam al-Rida and what is the reason behind it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) prohibits consuming the meat of those who differ in creed from the Shia, except in cases of necessity. He explains that this prohibition is based on Taqiyya (dissimulation), as the opposing sects also considered it permissible, so the prohibition served to distinguish the Shia from them.
